reasoning: All models that successfully analyzed the files found them safe. The PKGBUILD is a standard binary wrapper downloading from the project's own domain with SHA-256 checksum verification. The gaze-kde-bin.install script performs legitimate PAM integration tasks (enabling the module on install, cleaning up markers on removal) that align with the package's stated purpose. No malicious injection detected. The inconclusive results were due to API errors and parsing failures, not security concerns.
disagreement_analysis: No substantive disagreement on security. All successful analyses concluded safe. Inconclusive results stemmed from: (1) qwen3-235b API failure on install script, (2) deepseek-v4-flash providing thorough safe analysis but failing to output parseable XML tags, (3) openrouter/free outputting 'User Safety: safe' instead of proper XML for PKGBUILD. These are tooling/parsing issues, not security disagreements.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b failed to audit gaze-kde-bin.install due to HTTP 400 API error
deepseek-v4-flash analyzed install script thoroughly but output format was unparseable
openrouter/free failed to output parseable XML for PKGBUILD assessment
learnings: Models may provide correct security assessments in free-form text without using required XML tags; the parser should extract verdicts from natural language conclusions when XML is absent
API errors (HTTP 400) should trigger automatic retry or fallback to alternative models rather than marking files inconclusive
When a model's detailed analysis explicitly concludes 'safe' with thorough reasoning but fails XML parsing, the tool should recognize this as a valid safe verdict rather than inconclusive
